newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodian royalists say no force against faction.
newsitem.headline: Cambodian royalists say no force against faction.

text.p: A damaging split in Cambodia's royalist FUNCINPEC party continued to simmer on Monday but a senior party official said force would not be used against the renegade faction of his party.

FUNCINPEC leader, co-Premier Prince Norodom Ranariddh, has been insisting that eight breakaway members of parliament be expelled from the party and parliament and that the dissidents be banned from using the FUNCINPEC name and symbol.

The row within the royalist party has exacerbated the tense feud between Ranariddh and co-Premier Hun Sen and has virtualy paralysed government and forced the postponement of the regular parliamentary session, which should have opened on April 21.

There has been speculation in diplomatic circles that the split within FUNCINPEC was heading towards a confrontation but senior FUNCINPEC security official Serei Kosal said on Monday force would not be used against the renegades.
"There will be no explosion," Serei Kosal told a news conference. "FUNCINPEC respects realism, a stable society, the peaceful living of the people."

The eight MPs and other top royalist dissidents have challenged Ranariddh's leadership of the party with the support of Hun Sen, who does not support their expulsion from parliament or government posts.
But Serei Kosal warned that violence could occur if Cambodia's chronic political problems were not solved.
"Instability of society could lead to bloodshed. This is the danger," he said.
The FUNCINPEC renegades' headquarters in Phnom Penh, which still carried a FUNCINPEC party sign over its front door, was guarded by about 25 heavily armed troops on Monday.
